mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that rises by more than 0.4 percentage points from the previous month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: early-cycle or late-cycle labor market weakening
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE jumps by >0.4pp month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by > -0.5% for two straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and compresses valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS growth) above 1% month-over-month indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 1% AND RSAFS growth > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS grow >1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months, combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.2% month-over-month, signals a deepening labor market downturn that depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% for three consecutive months AND PAYEMS falls > -0.2% in the last month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative under the specified UNRATE and PAYEMS conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the housing starts index (HOUST) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as new housing construction signals broader economic activity and confidence, which supports near-term equity gains.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST changes and S&P 500 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over a rolling 3-year window.
